text:
Recent work supports testing richer negative sets, but hardness and false-negative risk require separate treatment. [Correcting the LogQ Correction (RecSys 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) revisits sampled softmax: ordinary logQ correction overlooks that the positive is always included, rather than sampled. Its revised objective treats positive inclusion explicitly and introduces an uncertainty-dependent sample weight. This addresses sampling bias; it does not identify latent positives. [gSASRec (IJCAI 2024 extended abstract)](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939) also links sparse negative sampling to overconfidence. These objective-level findings motivate experiments within BERT4Rec without changing its bidirectional masked-item backbone.

[R2NS (WWW 2026)](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) investigates recall and reranking of negative candidates, reporting improvements across five sequential backbones and two losses. False-negative-aware work takes a complementary direction: [SID4SRec (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0950705126010221) filters semantically overlapping sequence/item negatives, although its category/brand features are unavailable in this task. A practical hypothesis is mixed uniform and moderately hard negatives selected using the same BERT4Rec network, excluding known training positives and testing conservative downweighting of suspiciously similar candidates. Preserve masked-target training and appended-mask inference; compare against uniform sampled softmax and full softmax where affordable. These are experimental proposals, not evidence of gains on Industrial_and_Scientific or Electronics; selection must use the fixed four-category macro validation HR@10.
